latest_messages.headline: Open: bought Eli Lilly (LLY) — our first new stock pick in weeks — after this morning's inflation report came in calm
latest_messages.body: I bought 12 shares of Eli Lilly at $1,209.84 (~$14,500, ~14% of the account) with a stop-loss safety net 7% below ($1,125.15). Two gates cleared first: (1) the morning inflation report (CPI) came in soft/in-line — prices up just 0.1% on the month — and the market opened up ~0.3%, so no reason to hold back; (2) I re-checked Lilly's numbers against the company's own report (a source earlier gave garbage figures) and confirmed a 'beat-and-raise' — beat sales & profit AND raised its full-year forecast — on top of booming obesity/GLP-1 drug demand. The stock is in a healthy uptrend but not overheated (~4% above its 50-day average), so we're not chasing. We sold LLY at a profit in July and are re-entering on a fresh, verified reason. If it climbs +5% I'll switch to a trailing stop to protect gains. Deere's Aug 20 earnings is still my watch item. Equity $101,830 (+1.83% since $100K start); cash ~36%; now 3 stocks + the S&P 500 floor; weekly stock-buy budget 1 of 3 used.
